items.title: Crackdown on dangerous rented homes as new £7k fines kick in
items.summary: Councils can issue fines up to £7,000 from 22 June 2026 where Category 1 HHSRS hazards in rented homes are not remedied, as reported by GOV.UK.

items.title: Awaab's Law Phase 2: Guidance for social housing landlords
items.summary: Guidance for social landlords on Phase 2 of Awaab's Law, extending significant-hazard duties to seven further hazard groups from 30 November 2026, as reported by GOV.UK.

items.title: Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS) guidance
items.summary: New statutory HHSRS operating and enforcement guidance follows regulations that reduce the hazard list from 29 to 21, as reported by GOV.UK.

items.title: Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS): Case studies
items.summary: Illustrated case studies demonstrate how the revised HHSRS assessment and scoring process applies across the 21 hazards, as reported by GOV.UK.

items.title: Joseph Harvey & Anor v Polly Louise Heaver & Anor
items.source: Find Case Law, The National Archives
items.summary: The High Court found a let property unfit for human habitation under section 9A of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 and ordered specific performance.

items.title: Housing Ombudsman publishes revised Scheme and consultation outcome ahead of STAIRs
items.summary: The Ombudsman published the outcome of its STAIRs consultation and a revised Scheme, effective 1 October 2026, covering tenant information requests.

items.title: New Ombudsman report identifies lessons from monitoring the Complaint Handling Code
items.summary: The Ombudsman's first report from monitoring landlord compliance with the Complaint Handling Code identifies common weaknesses in complaint policies.

items.title: Housing disrepair claims
items.summary: A joint call for evidence on claims management activity in housing disrepair covered referral fees and solicitors' direct marketing; it closed on 12 February 2026.

items.title: Misuse of AI - Warning notice
items.summary: A warning notice reminds firms and solicitors that they remain accountable for AI outputs, including accurate citations and client confidentiality.

items.title: SRA issues AI usage warning notice
items.summary: Legal IT trade press reports the SRA's warning notice on AI misuse and the 42 reports of potential AI misuse received in a year.

items.title: Appeal for housing lawyers to continue late solicitor's 'invaluable' blog
items.summary: Following the death of housing lawyer Giles Peaker, Justin Bates KC appeals for volunteers to help continue his Nearly Legal blog, aiming to relaunch by October.
